title: Introduce contextual lint propagation, incremental test harness, and guarded release hook
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: slow and noisy presubmit runs and fragile release hooks were causing developer friction and occasional post-release rollbacks. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: (1) contextual lint propagation: lint runners now inherit repository context so linters run only against affected packages and their transitive boundaries, dramatically reducing noisy failures and runtime; (2) incremental test harness: a lightweight, language-agnostic harness that runs a fast subset of unit and integration tests locally and in CI by reusing cached virtualenvs/venvs and a file-change test map; (3) guarded release hook: a release orchestration step that performs staged release checks and provides an automatic safe-rollback pathway if downstream release verification fails. Summary of changes: consolidated lint entrypoints into ./ci/lint/entrypoint.sh and introduced a small Go shim (ci/lint/context-propagator) that computes impacted packages using git changed files and stored dependency metadata; added an incremental test runner (ci/test/incremental-runner.py) and a caching layer (ci/cache/test-cache-proxy) used by CI templates; refactored GitHub Actions workflows to include a lightweight "fastpath" lane that runs contextual lint + incremental tests and a full lane for merge-to-main snapshots; added a release job guard (ci/release/guarded_release_runner.go) which triggers a canary publish and wait/verify stage then either finalizes or triggers a rollback playbook; bumped eslint from 8.29.0 to 8.37.0 and pytest from 7.1.3 to 7.3.2 to pick up flaky-test fixes and new performance flags; included migration script scripts/migrate-locks.sh to reconcile package-lock/yarn.lock discrepancies and a small helper to export the change-to-test mapping (tools/gen-test-map). Backwards compatibility and rollout: changes are opt-in via repository-level config in .github/ci-config.yaml with sane defaults that preserve the existing behavior until teams flip the "fastpath_enabled" flag. Rollout plan included canary on redwood/examples and redwood-sdk-python for two weeks, then org-wide opt-in. Testing and validation: unit tests for the context propagator and guarded-release runner, integration smoke for the incremental runner, and end-to-end dry-run in ephemeral CI envs. Migration steps for integrators are documented in docs/ci/incremental-harness.md. Risks and mitigations: potential mismatch in test mapping for very large repositories was mitigated by a fallback to full test set when the mapping confidence score is low; release rollback logic has a manual confirmation toggle to avoid accidental rollbacks in emergency windows. Checklist: [x] tests added/updated [x] documentation updated [x] linear tickets linked [x] dependency bumps reviewed [x] rollout plan added. Related work: builds on ENG-4250 (presubmit fastpath proposal) and complements the presubmit cache work in ENG-4718.
